clue.text: It helps you see my relative from Paris hasn't second name

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the second of the two Ns in the French phrase is missing

parts.note: MON ONCLE is French for 'my uncle'

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a French uncle who has lost part of his name, oddly linked to seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: MON ONCLE has two Ns; 'hasn't second name' drops the second one, leaving MONOCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single eyeglass worn to improve vision.

clue.text: Should, say, mad lover frantically put on black?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece put on another sits beneath it, so the B follows
a frantic arrangement scrambles the letters of the words before it

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A frantic lover being told he should dress in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Should, say' looks like part of an instruction but is the definition: 'say' marks should as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Should is an example of a modal verb, the auxiliary that expresses obligation or possibility.

clue.text: Many cricket sides touring India

indicators.note: a touring side goes around the country, so these letters go around the next one

parts.note: LEG and ON are both names for the same half of a cricket field, the side the batsman stands on
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Lots of cricket teams on tour in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has teams visiting India; leg and on are in fact two names for the same half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a vast number, as in 'their fans are legion'.

clue.text: Red wine bottles for former president

indicators.note: to bottle something is to enclose it, so the wine holds the Red

parts.note: Pinot is a grape variety and its wine
Che Guevara was a famous communist, a Red

explanation.surface: A red wine that bottles up a former president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red wine' reads as one phrase, but 'Red' is a noun on its own: a communist revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusto Pinochet was Chile's military dictator and head of state from 1973 to 1990.

clue.text: Boy's characteristic in oddly ropy work

indicators.note: the phrase is placed in the middle of the rearranged letters
the four letters of the next word are put in an odd order

parts.note: a trait of a lad is a characteristic of a boy

explanation.surface: A boy's typical trait shows in some strangely stringy piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts a pick of odd letters, but here it rearranges ROPY into PORY, around TRAIT OF A LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portrait of a Lady is a celebrated novel by Henry James, a literary work.

clue.text: Chocolate highest ranked compiler hasn't finished

parts.note: number one, NO 1, written with I for the figure 1

indicators.note: the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a crossword compiler is a setter

explanation.surface: A top crossword compiler has left a chocolate half-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: NO 1 becomes NOI by reading the figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a chocolate made with hazelnuts, from the French for hazelnut.

clue.text: Rotten fellow, say, flipping bum

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: flipping turns the abbreviation over so it reads backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Someone calling a rotten man a flipping bum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like an insult noun but is the verb: to bum a cigarette is to cadge one. 'flipping' is mild British swearing in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is slang for scrounging it, getting it free by asking.

clue.text: Where Ruth is wrapped by Heather in blue material

indicators.note: the first piece sits inside the plant name, enclosed by it

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heather
the Book of Ruth is in the Old Testament, OT

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth wrapped up in a blue fabric by her friend Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth and Heather look like two women; Ruth is a book of the Bible and Heather is the plant, ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue, in British usage, means sexually explicit, and erotica is such writing or art.

clue.text: Extra clothing huge and blue

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: more means additional, extra
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Someone feeling down about needing extra-large clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue and being morose both mean gloomy and sullen.

clue.text: Rushed to swallow last of aioli dip, showing precipitation

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the next letter goes into the verb

parts.note: ran is a synonym for rushed

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: a garlic mayonnaise; its last letter is I
a drop is a dip or fall

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to wolf down the end of the aioli dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A raindrop is a single unit of rain, the commonest form of precipitation.

clue.text: Puritan using speech to probe film

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so the first word enters the second

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like mist on glass
oral means spoken, using speech

explanation.surface: A puritanical censor speaking out to investigate a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is a movie in the surface but a thin haze in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is strict about morals, as a moralist is, preaching right conduct to others.

clue.text: It's used when blinking loud cry briefly interrupts festival

indicators.note: the cry breaks into the middle of the festival word

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival

indicators.note: a brief version is cut short by one letter at the end

parts.note: a yell is a loud cry

explanation.surface: A shout cutting into a festival, with blinking lights perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Blinking is the rapid closing and opening of the eyelid, the skin fold over the eye.

clue.text: Pig by borders of Indiana state

parts.note: a pig, figuratively, is a slovenly person, a sloven

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word, its first and last

parts.note: a US state; its borders are I and A

explanation.surface: A pig standing near the edges of Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: Indiana suggests a US state, but the state needed is in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is an independent European country, a nation state.

clue.text: Where US criminals are ready for release

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'the can' is American slang for prison
second meaning: a film that is finished and awaiting release is ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'release' makes the second half sound like freedom from jail, but it is a film's release.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both locked up in jail, in US slang, and completed, used of filmed footage.

clue.text: Drug case stirring up memories

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: A drug case in court bringing back old memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal but is grammatical: the vocative is a noun case in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocative describes something that calls feelings or recollections vividly to mind.

clue.text: Maybe Plato turned up in boring trio of articles

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the reversed word goes inside the articles

parts.note: the three English articles A, THE and AN

indicators.note: in a down answer, a word turned up reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Plato showing up somewhere among three dull articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull in the surface but means piercing into; the trio is the full set of English articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was born in and taught at Athens, so he is an example of a citizen of that city.

clue.text: Stand in circle around Scottish island in game

indicators.note: the stand-in and the circle together go around the island's name

parts.note: a sub is a substitute, a stand-in
O is the shape of a circle
Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: Standing in a circle on a Scottish island playing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Subbuteo is a British table football game played by flicking small figures.

clue.text: Unlikely Victor dismisses good cook perfunctorily

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an underdog is the side not expected to win

explanation.surface: An unlikely winner sacks a good chef who cooks carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To underdo food is to give it too little cooking time, a careless or hasty preparation.

clue.text: Stink about Republican associating with explosive, volatile element

indicators.note: the explosive piece joins on after the first part
the smell wraps around the next letter

parts.note: BO is body odour
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: A political row about a Republican linked to explosives and a volatile situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromine is a chemical element, a liquid that readily gives off choking fumes.

clue.text: Fine service by jester for king?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an ace is an unreturnable tennis serve
a card is a joker, an amusing person

explanation.surface: A jester performing a fine service for his king.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the king as an example, the playing card rather than a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of playing cards the king is one of the court cards bearing a picture of a figure.

clue.text: Short person driving around middle of fairway

indicators.note: the driver goes around the letter

parts.note: a cabby is a taxi driver

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word

parts.note: its middle letter is R

explanation.surface: A short golfer driving off around the middle of the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of a person but means short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Short in the sense of curt or irritable matches crabby, bad-tempered.

clue.text: Resembling fare the Spanish offer, east to west

indicators.note: an across answer read toward the west runs right to left, backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a bid is an offer
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Something like food the Spanish offer, travelling east to west.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is food, so something edible has the quality of food, fit to be eaten.

clue.text: Bust, or the opposite — investing succeeded!

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the boom wraps the letter

parts.note: the opposite of bust, in economic terms, is boom
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: An economic boom-or-bust story about successful investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' is the economic slump in the surface and the chest as the definition; 'boom' is its economic opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust and a bosom are both words for a woman's chest.

clue.text: Lag's processing date, clad in green

indicators.note: the rearranged word is dressed in the colour, enclosed by it

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

indicators.note: processing puts the letters through a change, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A convict, a lag, dealing with a date while dressed in green.
explanation.walkthrough: A lag is British slang for a convict, which is the surface sense; the definition is lag as a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead time is the delay between starting a process and its completion, a time lag.

clue.text: Shakespeare character leaves to eat with princess

parts.note: cress is a salad plant whose leaves are eaten
Princess Ida is the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean figure who departs to dine with a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb, departs, but is the noun for foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida is the faithless heroine of Shakespeare's play Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Slow-witted bishop possibly sheepish

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ovine means sheep-like, a playful sense of sheepish

explanation.surface: A dim bishop looking somewhat embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepish' means embarrassed in the surface but literally like a sheep, OVINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovine literally means cow-like, and figuratively dull and slow in thought.

clue.text: Standard hotel not found in accessible old province

parts.note: a norm is a standard

indicators.note: the letter is absent from the next word

parts.note: handy means convenient, easily reached
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A standard hotel missing from an easy-to-reach old French region.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy was a historic province of northern France, now divided into departments.
